p07-ctx-t.text: **Used on this page**: $J=\sum\max(0,-y_i\mathbf{v}^T\mathbf{a}_i)$; one mistake adds $\rho\|\mathbf{a}_i\|^2$ to its score; when $\mathbf{v}=\mathbf{0}$, all scores are 0.

p07-c2-t.text:

[Correction] $J=0$ is not enough to stop: at $\mathbf{v}=\mathbf{0}$, $J=0$ yet no point is correct
So the stop test must check $Y=\emptyset$ directly

steps.label: Goal: merge all misclassified… · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes: Goal: merge all misclassified… · 1/3 · Female: The last unit only showed how to use a line. If the line is misplaced, the data must give the direction of correction. Predict: when several samples are wrong, do we fix them one by one, or all together?

narration.label: s1.mp3
narration.transcript: Female: The last unit only showed how to use a line. If the line is misplaced, the data must give the direction of correction. Predict: when several samples are wrong, do we fix them one by one, or all together?

steps.label: Goal: merge all misclassified… · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Goal: merge all misclassified… · 2/3 · Male: This unit takes three steps. Find all misclassified samples, add up the corrections each one asks for, and update the weights only once, then plug in the new weights to check the scores.

narration.label: s2.mp3
narration.transcript: Male: This unit takes three steps. Find all misclassified samples, add up the corrections each one asks for, and update the weights only once, then plug in the new weights to check the scores.

steps.label: Goal: merge all misclassified… · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Goal: merge all misclassified… · 3/3 · Female: Take this away: this unit adds up all mistakes and updates the weights only once. Next page, we first fold the intercept into the inner product.

narration.label: s3.mp3
narration.transcript: Female: Take this away: this unit adds up all mistakes and updates the weights only once. Next page, we first fold the intercept into the inner product.

steps.label: Augmented vectors: score times… · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes: Augmented vectors: score times… · 1/3 · Male: First, fold the intercept in. Append a 1 to the sample x to get the augmented sample a, and append the bias b to w to get v, so the score is v times a. Guess: if the score is exactly zero, is it correct?

narration.label: s4.mp3
narration.transcript: Male: First, fold the intercept in. Append a 1 to the sample x to get the augmented sample a, and append the bias b to w to get v, so the score is v times a. Guess: if the score is exactly zero, is it correct?

steps.label: Augmented vectors: score times… · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Augmented vectors: score times… · 2/3 · Female: No. Multiply the score by the true label y, plus 1 for positive and minus 1 for negative. Only when this labeled score is above zero is the sample strictly correct; zero or negative needs a correction.

narration.label: s5.mp3
narration.transcript: Female: No. Multiply the score by the true label y, plus 1 for positive and minus 1 for negative. Only when this labeled score is above zero is the sample strictly correct; zero or negative needs a correction.

steps.label: Augmented vectors: score times… · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Augmented vectors: score times… · 3/3 · Male: Take this away: a sample is strictly correct only if its labeled score is above zero. Next page, we gather the samples that need correcting.

narration.label: s6.mp3
narration.transcript: Male: Take this away: a sample is strictly correct only if its labeled score is above zero. Next page, we gather the samples that need correcting.

steps.label: Mistake set Y: add positive… · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes: Mistake set Y: add positive… · 1/3 · Female: Think of a tug-of-war: only those on the wrong side ask for a correction. They go into the set Y, including points right on the boundary. Predict: do positive and negative mistakes ask for the same direction?

narration.label: s7.mp3
narration.transcript: Female: Think of a tug-of-war: only those on the wrong side ask for a correction. They go into the set Y, including points right on the boundary. Predict: do positive and negative mistakes ask for the same direction?

steps.label: Mistake set Y: add positive… · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Mistake set Y: add positive… · 2/3 · Male: No. A positive mistake asks to add itself, a negative mistake asks to subtract itself. The loss J is the sum of those mistakes' scores, and with the set fixed, its derivative is their sum.

narration.label: s8.mp3
narration.transcript: Male: No. A positive mistake asks to add itself, a negative mistake asks to subtract itself. The loss J is the sum of those mistakes' scores, and with the set fixed, its derivative is their sum.

steps.label: Mistake set Y: add positive… · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Mistake set Y: add positive… · 3/3 · Female: Take this away: positive mistakes ask to be added, negative mistakes ask to be subtracted. Remember tug-of-war is only a metaphor; the line does not shift by the same distance. Next page, we write the correction as an update rule.

narration.label: s9.mp3
narration.transcript: Female: Take this away: positive mistakes ask to be added, negative mistakes ask to be subtracted. Remember tug-of-war is only a metaphor; the line does not shift by the same distance. Next page, we write the correction as an update rule.

steps.label: Batch update: sum all… · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes: Batch update: sum all… · 1/3 · Male: The update is: the next v equals v plus the learning rate times the sum of y times a over all mistakes. Think: why must the whole set be decided by the same old weights?

narration.label: s10.mp3
narration.transcript: Male: The update is: the next v equals v plus the learning rate times the sum of y times a over all mistakes. Think: why must the whole set be decided by the same old weights?

steps.label: Batch update: sum all… · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Batch update: sum all… · 2/3 · Female: Because batch update means: use fixed old weights to find the whole batch of mistakes, add the corrections, and change the weights once at the end. Add positives, subtract negatives; delta equal to minus y is just another way to write it.

narration.label: s11.mp3
narration.transcript: Female: Because batch update means: use fixed old weights to find the whole batch of mistakes, add the corrections, and change the weights once at the end. Add positives, subtract negatives; delta equal to minus y is just another way to write it.

steps.label: Batch update: sum all… · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Batch update: sum all… · 3/3 · Male: Take this away: a batch update finds all mistakes with the old weights, sums them, and updates once. Next page, we work through the source example.

narration.label: s12.mp3
narration.transcript: Male: Take this away: a batch update finds all mistakes with the old weights, sums them, and updates once. Next page, we work through the source example.

steps.label: Example 3.1: find two mistakes… · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes: Example 3.1: find two mistakes… · 1/3 · Female: The dashed line is the old boundary. Positive A at 0.4, 0.05 scores minus 0.05, so it is wrong. Negative B at minus 0.2, 0.75 scores 0.05, also wrong. Predict the total correction.

narration.label: s13.mp3
narration.transcript: Female: The dashed line is the old boundary. Positive A at 0.4, 0.05 scores minus 0.05, so it is wrong. Negative B at minus 0.2, 0.75 scores 0.05, also wrong. Predict the total correction.

steps.label: Example 3.1: find two mistakes… · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Example 3.1: find two mistakes… · 2/3 · Male: A is positive and asks to add itself; B is negative and asks to subtract itself. The sum of the deltas is minus A's augmented vector plus B's augmented vector, giving minus 0.6, 0.7, 0. The last entry cancels by coincidence in this example.

narration.label: s14.mp3
narration.transcript: Male: A is positive and asks to add itself; B is negative and asks to subtract itself. The sum of the deltas is minus A's augmented vector plus B's augmented vector, giving minus 0.6, 0.7, 0. The last entry cancels by coincidence in this example.

steps.label: Example 3.1: find two mistakes… · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Example 3.1: find two mistakes… · 3/3 · Female: Take this away: the two corrections add up to a total of minus 0.6, 0.7, 0. Next page, we multiply by the learning rate and update.

narration.label: s15.mp3
narration.transcript: Female: Take this away: the two corrections add up to a total of minus 0.6, 0.7, 0. Next page, we multiply by the learning rate and update.

steps.label: Example 3.1 after the update: A… · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes: Example 3.1 after the update: A… · 1/3 · Male: Multiply the total correction by 0.7 and subtract from v0 to get the new weights 1.42, 0.51, minus 0.5. Predict: will the solid new boundary classify both A and B correctly?

narration.label: s16.mp3
narration.transcript: Male: Multiply the total correction by 0.7 and subtract from v0 to get the new weights 1.42, 0.51, minus 0.5. Predict: will the solid new boundary classify both A and B correctly?

steps.label: Example 3.1 after the update: A… · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Example 3.1 after the update: A… · 2/3 · Female: A's new score is 1.42 times 0.4 plus 0.51 times 0.05 minus 0.5, which is 0.0935, above zero. B's new score is minus 0.4015, below zero. The other six points also stay on the correct side.

narration.label: s17.mp3
narration.transcript: Female: A's new score is 1.42 times 0.4 plus 0.51 times 0.05 minus 0.5, which is 0.0935, above zero. B's new score is minus 0.4015, below zero. The other six points also stay on the correct side.

steps.label: Example 3.1 after the update: A… · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Example 3.1 after the update: A… · 3/3 · Male: Take this away: one batch update moved both mistakes to the correct side. But this is one successful example, not a guarantee. Next page, the common myths.

narration.label: s18.mp3
narration.transcript: Male: Take this away: one batch update moved both mistakes to the correct side. But this is one successful example, not a guarantee. Next page, the common myths.

steps.label: Myth: one correction always… · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes: Myth: one correction always… · 1/3 · Female: Two myths. First, does one correction always lower the error count? Second, can we stop when the loss is zero? The left card is the wrong idea, the right card is the correct practice. Think: what happens when the weights are the zero vector?

narration.label: s19.mp3
narration.transcript: Female: Two myths. First, does one correction always lower the error count? Second, can we stop when the loss is zero? The left card is the wrong idea, the right card is the correct practice. Think: what happens when the weights are the zero vector?

steps.label: Myth: one correction always… · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Myth: one correction always… · 2/3 · Male: With zero weights, every score is zero and the loss is zero, yet no point is strictly correct. So the stop test must check directly whether the mistake set is empty. A batch update also has cross effects between samples, so the error count need not fall.

narration.label: s20.mp3
narration.transcript: Male: With zero weights, every score is zero and the loss is zero, yet no point is strictly correct. So the stop test must check directly whether the mistake set is empty. A batch update also has cross effects between samples, so the error count need not fall.

steps.label: Myth: one correction always… · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Myth: one correction always… · 3/3 · Female: Take this away: stop when the mistake set is empty, not merely when the loss is zero. Next page, your turn to compute with learning rate 0.5.

narration.label: s21.mp3
narration.transcript: Female: Take this away: stop when the mistake set is empty, not merely when the loss is zero. Next page, your turn to compute with learning rate 0.5.

steps.label: Practice: learning rate 0.5; new… · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes: Practice: learning rate 0.5; new… · 1/3 · Male: Your turn. Keep the total correction minus 0.6, 0.7, 0, and change only the learning rate to 0.5. Find the new weights and the new scores of A and B. Hint: keep the total, change only the multiplier in front.

narration.label: s22.mp3
narration.transcript: Male: Your turn. Keep the total correction minus 0.6, 0.7, 0, and change only the learning rate to 0.5. Find the new weights and the new scores of A and B. Hint: keep the total, change only the multiplier in front.

steps.label: Practice: learning rate 0.5; new… · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Practice: learning rate 0.5; new… · 2/3 · Female: The new weights are 1.3 and 0.65, with bias still minus 0.5. A's new score is 0.0525 and B's is minus 0.2725, so both are correct.

narration.label: s23.mp3
narration.transcript: Female: The new weights are 1.3 and 0.65, with bias still minus 0.5. A's new score is 0.0525 and B's is minus 0.2725, so both are correct.

steps.label: Practice: learning rate 0.5; new… · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Practice: learning rate 0.5; new… · 3/3 · Male: Take this away: with 0.5 times the total correction, A and B are still classified correctly. But one success is not a general guarantee. The next unit asks: if the data are separable, why can't we keep correcting forever?

narration.label: s24.mp3
